statement: Tom has 50 cents. He buys a ball for 30 cents. Then his gran gives him 20 cents. How much money does Tom have now?

choices.misconception: I worked out what Tom had after buying the ball and forgot that his gran gave him 20 cents.
I mixed up the steps: I added the price of the ball and took away the money from his gran.
I added the 20 cents from his gran but forgot that Tom spent 30 cents on the ball.
I added all the amounts together: 50 + 30 + 20.

hints: Follow Tom's money one step at a time.
Money spent makes Tom's amount go down, and money given makes it go up. Start with 50 cents, change it after the ball, then change it again after his gran's gift.
After buying the ball, Tom has 50 - 30 = 20 cents.

solutions.reliable: Tom starts with 50 cents. The ball costs 30 cents, so he has 50 - 30 = 20 cents left. His gran gives him 20 cents, so he has 20 + 20 = 40 cents. The idea to keep: in a money story, take away what is spent and add what is given, in order.
solutions.elegant: The 20 cents from his gran makes up for most of the 30 cents he spent, so overall Tom is 10 cents down: 50 - 10 = 40 cents. The idea to keep: you can put the changes together first, then use them once.

whyOnTest: Money and change: one amount is spent and another is received, so each step must go the right way.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
